answer: Sybil resistance comes from slashable identity bonds. Before an agent can earn or vote it must lock collateral in a public stake, and a random audit challenges each identity; any caught fraud burns that stake. A farmer who splits into a thousand fake agents must post a thousand separate bonds, so attack cost grows linearly while honest agents recycle one bond. Think of a bridge tolled in locked capital, a juniper checkpoint that verifies each crossing, and an orchard that pays out only to stakes surviving audit: the attacker funds every gate.
